channel.title: nexusEVnews
channel.description: Independent EV and renewable energy news, curated daily. Electric vehicles, solar, battery tech, and charging infrastructure.

item.title: The BMW iX Still Has Tricks the iX3 Can't Match, But the Price Gap Is Hard to Justify
item.dc:creator: Autogefühl
item.description: Thomas and Lea run the facelifted BMW iX on a full German Autobahn road trip. Real-world mixed range came in around 480 km, roughly 120 km behind the iX3 under the same conditions, and the 195 kW charging peak adds up to a 30-minute stop versus the iX3's 21 minutes.

item.title: Rivian's Spin-Off Built a 100-Mile E-Bike With No Chain and Automotive-Grade Ambitions
item.dc:creator: MotorTrend Channel
item.description: The Also TMB is a pedal-by-wire electric bike that spun out of Rivian, using Rivian R1 battery cells and a series-hybrid drivetrain with no mechanical chain. Starting at $3,500, it weighs 80 lbs, claims 100 miles of range, and tops out at 28 mph assisted.

item.title: You Know BYD Means Business When Daniel Craig Is Narrating the Ad
item.dc:creator: BYD Global
item.description: BYD's premium DENZA brand released a global brand film featuring Daniel Craig. No specs, no range figures, just a cinematic minute about change and new roads, signaling where BYD intends to compete next.

item.title: The $25,000 Electric Truck Made in Indiana That You're Allowed to Fix Yourself
item.dc:creator: Jay Leno's Garage
item.description: Jay Leno drives a prototype of the Slate truck, a modular electric pickup priced in the mid-$20,000s, built in Warsaw, Indiana. It has exposed fasteners, no paint, a composite body, and explicit right-to-repair support including DIY warranty repairs through a 4,000-shop independent service network.

item.title: A Quiet Forest Night With a BYD Sealion 7 and an Attached Tent: No Agenda
item.dc:creator: FISH13
item.description: A BYD Sealion 7 powers the Arbor Outdoor HEXONA tent for a quiet forest overnight with no talking and no range test. Vehicle-to-load EV camping done in a calm, ASMR style. Contains paid promotion for BYD Korea and Arbor Outdoor.

item.title: Two Batteries, One Hitch, and the Case for All-Electric Glamping
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: The Lightship AE1 carries its own 69 kWh battery and 80 kW motor to neutralize trailer drag on the tow vehicle. Paired with a Rivian, the real-world efficiency numbers are hard to argue with. This is what all-electric glamping looks like when the hardware actually works.

item.title: Rivian Has an Uber Robotaxi Deal, a DoorDash Bot Spinoff, and Made the $20,000 VW ID.1 Possible
item.dc:creator: Munro Live
item.description: RJ Scaringe confirmed a deal with Uber to build a robotaxi on the R2 platform and described DoorDash delivery bots being built by Rivian spinoff ALSO. He also explained how the same zonal computing architecture behind the R1 and R2 let Volkswagen engineer the ID.1 at a roughly $20,000 price point.

item.title: Scout's Traveler and Terra Get a Style Refresh. The 2027 Production Target Hasn't Changed.
item.dc:creator: The Fast Lane Car
item.description: The Traveler wears a new matte white called White Cap with 20-inch wheels and 35-inch KO3 tires, and the brick-red interior is the most complete cabin look yet. Running and driving mules are in cold-weather testing in Europe. Production is still on for 2027, deliveries in 2028, and 85% of reservations are the range-extended Harvester trim.

item.title: Sierro Is a Plug-In Home Battery Backup That Skips the Electrician
item.dc:creator: Kim Java
item.description: Sierro is a plug-in LFP home battery that plugs into a standard outlet, switches over in under 15 milliseconds during a power outage, and supports MPPT solar charging. Rated for 8,000 cycles with a five-year warranty and no installation required.

item.title: Wayve CEO on Why Licensing Its AI Driver Is the Biggest Bet in Autonomous Vehicles
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg Technology
item.description: Wayve's CEO argued that licensing its AI driving platform to automakers represents a larger market than building cars or running robotaxi fleets. A live demonstration in London's Kings Cross used six cameras and one radar with no maps, and the safety driver's hands stayed off the wheel throughout.

item.title: The Chevrolet Bolt Is Back, and It's Still the Best-Value EV You Can Buy
item.dc:creator: Edmunds Cars
item.description: Edmunds tested the returning Chevrolet Bolt and found 290 real-world miles against a 262-mile EPA estimate, a starting price just under $29,000, NACS charging that runs three times faster than the previous generation, and a chassis that still surprises at this price point.

item.title: Tesla Semi's Series Production Model, Explained by the Engineer Behind It
item.dc:creator: Out of Spec Reviews
item.description: Kyle Conner and Tesla Semi program lead Dan Priestley walk through the changes from the early beta fleet to the current series production truck, covering the new 4680 battery pack, MCS 3.2 charging standard, dual-axle drivetrain design, and the 25 kW ePTO port being standardized for electric trailer equipment.

item.title: Porsche Taycan Turbo GT with Manthey Kit Sets New EV Record at the Nürburgring
item.dc:creator: Porsche
item.description: On-board footage from Lars Kern's 6:55.533 Nordschleife record lap on April 15, beating the previous electric executive car record by more than nine seconds. The Manthey Kit is the first developed for an electric Porsche and covers aerodynamics, powertrain, brakes, suspension, and wheels.

item.title: Waymo and Zoox Are Competing for the Ride-Hailing Market. The Economics Are Still Being Worked Out.
item.dc:creator: Financial Times
item.description: The FT examines how Waymo and Amazon-owned Zoox are reshaping urban ride-hailing, with Waymo logging 127 million driverless miles with no fatal crashes and robo taxi fares running roughly a third above comparable Uber rides in San Francisco.

item.title: Lexus Reveals the 2027 TZ: A Three-Row Electric SUV Built Around Cabin Silence and V2H Power
item.dc:creator: REC Anything
item.description: Lexus unveiled the 2027 TZ at Toyota's Technical Center in Japan, presenting a three-row BEV with V2H bidirectional charging, a 5.2-second 0-100 km/h time, 3,500 lb towing capacity, and access to the NACS Supercharger network.

item.title: Rivian's CEO on R2, AI-Defined Vehicles, and Why Every Automaker Needs a Software Platform
item.dc:creator: The Electric Duo
item.description: RJ Scaringe speaks at ACT Expo about ramping the $45,000 R2, the $5.8 billion Volkswagen software licensing deal, Amazon's 30,000-plus electric vans, and his argument that a connected, self-driving platform will be a prerequisite for market share by 2035.

item.title: How a Japanese Climate Activist Got 17 Coal Projects Cancelled and What She's Building Next
item.dc:creator: TED
item.description: Kimiko Hirata's multi-year campaign against coal expansion in Japan led to 17 project cancellations totaling 9 gigawatts, Japan's first shareholder climate activism at Mizuho bank, and a new think tank building the affirmative case for 90 percent renewables.

item.title: VW, BMW, and Mercedes Are Running Full Urban Driver Assistance in China. Western Buyers Don't Get It.
item.dc:creator: Out of Spec Reviews
item.description: Out of Spec Reviews drives the Volkswagen ID Era 9X through Beijing traffic on the Momenta driver assistance system, which also runs in BMW and Mercedes vehicles in China. The result is comparable to Tesla FSD. Western markets get Travel Assist.

item.title: A Solar EV Charger That Arrives on a Truck, Needs No Foundations, and Pays Back the Hospital That Owns It
item.dc:creator: Everything Electric TECH
item.description: 3TI's Halo FastHub installs at a Manchester hospital in three days with no concrete foundations, solar supplementing 30 to 40 percent of charging, and revenue from electricity sales going back to the hospital that owns the units.

item.title: Atlanta, Rivian, and the Quiet Coincidence
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: Atlanta has a failing air quality grade and a Rivian plant on its doorstep. A hypothetical about what one city could do with the electric mobility infrastructure that already exists — R2 autonomous taxis, ALSO cargo quads, e-bikes, and ZTL-style restricted zones — and what the health data says the stakes actually are. Includes data from the HEI lockdown air quality study (Chen et al., 2025) and the American Lung Association's 2025 Atlanta air quality report.
